title: RL for Games — AlphaZero, MuZero, and the LLM-Reasoning Era

questions.question: GRPO drops PPO's critic. What plays the role of the baseline instead?
options: A running average of all rewards seen so far in training
The reward model's score for the reference policy's completion
The mean reward over the G completions sampled for that prompt, normalized by the group std
The value estimate at the previous token position, bootstrapped one step at a time as in TD learning
questions.explanation: Sampling a group per prompt gives you an unbiased, on-the-spot estimate of that prompt's expected reward, which is precisely what a critic was approximating. Being per-prompt also makes it robust to prompts of wildly different difficulty.

questions.question: How does the quality of the group baseline scale with group size G?
options: The variance of the group mean falls like 1/G, so its standard error falls like 1/√G
The variance of the group mean falls like 1/√G, so its standard error falls like 1/G, which is why doubling G halves the advantage noise
Both the variance of the group mean and its standard error fall like 1/√G, so the two rates are the same
Neither depends on G — raising G changes only the bias of the group baseline, never its spread
questions.explanation: Var(mean of G iid samples) = σ²/G, and standard error is its square root. Mixing the two rates up is why people over-estimate the gain from doubling G — going 8 → 64 cuts the error by about 2.8×, not 8×.

questions.question: What is MuZero's advance over AlphaZero?
options: It replaces MCTS with a policy-gradient update on a group-relative advantage, so search disappears from both training and inference
It learns a latent dynamics model and searches inside it, so the environment's rules need not be known
It adds a learned reward model so the same loop can be trained from human preferences instead of from game outcomes
It drops the value head and trains only on the MCTS visit distribution, which is what lets it plan without knowing the rules
questions.explanation: AlphaZero's MCTS calls a real simulator, which is only available when the rules are given. Learning h/g/f lets the same loop plan in latent space, which is how one algorithm covers Go, chess and Atari.

questions.question: The KL penalty's gradient with respect to softmax logits is d KL/dz_i = p_i·(log(p_i/q_i) − KL). Why is KL subtracted inside the parentheses?
options: To keep every component non-negative, since the KL itself is non-negative by Jensen's inequality and a negative component would reward drift
To cancel the 1/G factor that the group-relative term introduces
Because softmax normalization means every valid logit gradient must sum to zero, and the −KL term is what makes Σ_i vanish
To make the penalty invariant to the group size G
questions.explanation: Σ_i p_i·log(p_i/q_i) is the KL itself, so Σ_i p_i·(log(p_i/q_i) − KL) = KL − KL = 0. Dropping the −KL leaves a term that shifts all logits by the same amount — a no-op for the distribution that still corrupts the update's scale.

questions.question: DeepSeekMath argues GRPO suits reasoning better than PPO. Which of these is NOT one of its reasons?
options: No value network to train, which roughly halves optimizer memory
The group baseline handles a single reward delivered only at the end of the trajectory
Per-prompt normalization makes advantages comparable across problems of very different difficulty
The group samples can be reused for many epochs, unlike PPO's rollouts
questions.explanation: Multi-epoch reuse is PPO's contribution via the clipped ratio, not GRPO's; GRPO still needs fresh on-policy groups. The other three are exactly the arguments in the paper.

questions.question: What distinguishes R1-Zero from R1?
options: R1-Zero applies GRPO to the base model with rule-based rewards: strong reasoning, unreadable language-mixed CoT. R1 adds cold-start SFT and rejection sampling for readability
R1-Zero is one of the six distilled dense models released in the paper, spanning Qwen-1.5B to Llama-70B; R1 is the mixture-of-experts teacher whose reasoning traces they were fine-tuned on
R1-Zero scores completions with a learned reward model; R1 replaces it with a rule-based verifier that checks the final answer and the <think> formatting
R1-Zero runs MCTS over reasoning steps with a process reward model; R1 drops the search and trains on full rollouts instead
questions.explanation: R1-Zero is the ablation proving reasoning emerges from RL alone, with no SFT anywhere in the pipeline. Its cost is presentation quality, which is what R1's four-stage pipeline exists to repair.
